# --instructions--

Write a function `groupByLength(words)` that returns a `Map` where each key is a word length (a number) and its value is an array with all the words of that length, in the order they appear in `words`

# --asserts--

`groupByLength(["sun", "moon", "sky", "star"])` must map `3` to `["sun", "sky"]`.

```javascript
tryCatch(JSON.stringify(groupByLength(["sun", "moon", "sky", "star"]).get(3)) === '["sun","sky"]');
```

`groupByLength(["sun", "moon", "sky", "star"])` must map `4` to `["moon", "star"]`.

```javascript
tryCatch(JSON.stringify(groupByLength(["sun", "moon", "sky", "star"]).get(4)) === '["moon","star"]');
```

The keys must be numbers, so `get("3")` must return `undefined`.

```javascript
tryCatch(groupByLength(["sun", "moon", "sky", "star"]).get("3") === undefined);
```

`groupByLength([])` must have `0` pairs.

```javascript
tryCatch(groupByLength([]).size === 0);
```

# --solutions--

```javascript
function groupByLength(words) {
  let groups = new Map();
  for (const word of words) {
    if (!groups.has(word.length)) {
      groups.set(word.length, []);
    }
    groups.get(word.length).push(word);
  }
  return groups;
}
```
